narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>Five rods in a row can only mean forty one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Without a space, nobody can see where the tens end.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The reader has to guess how the rods are split.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows five upright rods with the label 41 only; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>To check a reading, split the rods and add up each place's value.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Then ask yourself whether another split gives a different number.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>If it does, the numeral needs a clear way to mark its places.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; check lines appear: split the rods and add each place; try another split

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu says five rods in a row can only mean forty one. Without a space, the row can be split in many ways, each giving a different number.
